```haskell
module Main (main) where

import Data.List (foldl')

main :: IO ()
main = do
  inp <- getContents
  case map read (words inp) :: [Integer] of
    (m:n:_) -> print (go m n)
    _ -> return ()
  where
    go m n = last (foldl' step (replicate (fromIntegral n) 1) [2 .. m])
    step dp _ = scanl1 (+) dp
```

Wait — the DP update in C++ is `dp[col] += dp[col-1]`, which is exactly a prefix sum (scanl1 (+)). Correct. But note the row loop runs for row=2..m, i.e., m-1 times. `foldl' step dp [2..m]` does that. Edge case m=1: no iterations, answer 1. Good.
